target.statement: O-DisCo-Edit attains the best normalized average score (0.7553) for the Object Removal (49-frame) task on the OmnimatteRF benchmark, surpassing MiniMax-Remover (0.4816), ProPainter (0.4844) and DiffuEraser (0.2682).
target.dataset: OmnimatteRF benchmark for object removal (49-frame videos, 480x720)

code_links: https://cyqii.github.io/O-DisCo-Edit.github.io/ (project page only; no GitHub/repo or weights linked in the paper)

compute.basis: The target requires running a CogVideoX-I2V (5B-class DiT, 49 frames at 720x480) with two additional LoRAs plus the whole baseline suite (VACE 1.3B/14B, MiniMax-Remover, ProPainter, DiffuEraser), none of which is released, so the run cannot even be started on a CPU laptop; the vram/ref_minutes figures are the estimated GPU-class cost, not a laptop-feasible cost.

blockers: No code, no model weights, no checkpoints released ('In the future, we will make our model publicly available')
Trained on ~180k Senorita-2M video-mask pairs on 8xA800 GPUs (2400 + 5150 steps, batch 32) - retraining infeasible on a laptop
Inference needs a GPU (CogVideoX 5B-class DiT at 720x480x49 frames); CPU inference would take days per clip
The curated benchmark (134 sets from DIVAS/VPData) and its masks are not released; reference first frames were produced with HiDream-E1 and a commercial model (Jimeng), so inputs are not reproducible
Headline number is a normalized average over metrics that require re-running VACE 14B, Senorita, VideoPainter and removal baselines (many A100/V100-class GPU-hours)
title: O-DisCo-Edit: Object Distortion Control for Unified Realistic Video Editing
